newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas recovers on impending cold front.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas recovers on impending cold front.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices recovered from yesterday's lows on Tuesday, as another cold front was poised to arrive in the central U.S. this weekend, market sources said.
Swing prices on the Gulf Coast pipes regained about 10 cents to the $2.50s, with Henry Hub, La., quoted in the high-$2.50s to low-$2.60s.
Prices were equally higher in south Texas, where traders reported closing deals mostly in the low-$2.40s amid near-normal temperatures.
Despite the continuance of above-normal temperatures in the East, prices at the New York city-gate remained fairly steady around $3 per mmBtu.
On the Appalachian pipes, however, stronger Gulf values lifted prices by more than five cents to the $2.70s and $2.80s.
The East is expected to experience cooler temperatures this weekend and into next week, Weather Services Corp reported.
In the Midcontinent, prices rose by an average of 10 cents to the high-$2.30s to high-$2.40s as colder temperatures were expected to arrive in the region later this week.
However, Chicago city-gate values were talked lower in the $2.74-2.80 range.
Six- to 10-day forecasts are calling for below- to much below-normal temperatures across the Northwest and the mid-section of the U.S.
In west Texas, Permian prices jumped into the low-to-mid $2.30s, gaining about five cents from Monday.
Swing prices at the southern California border were also about five cents higher in the low-$2.40s.
